Holding the federal funds rate at 5.25–5.50% while continuing QT keeps policy restrictively biased even as inflation eases. The Financial Stability Report (FSR) supports the statement’s characterization of a “sound and resilient” banking system but flags vulnerabilities that could amplify the restraining effects of tight policy: higher long-term rates and an elevated term premium that can trigger market-liquidity strains; structural fragilities in nonbank intermediation (money market funds and hedge fund leverage in Treasury basis trades); rising credit risk in CRE—especially office—and in leveraged loans; and geopolitical and China-related growth risks. Offsetting these are solid bank capital and liquidity, stabilization of deposits by mid-2023, and the Bank Term Funding Program backstop. On net, resilience tempers tail risks, but tighter financial conditions plus noted vulnerabilities keep the tone cautiously negative.
